title: Your own voice
job: An eight-sentence piece that changes register midway
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: <four sentences, register A> + <pivot> + <four sentences, register B>

rules.text: Spanish marks a change of register with an explicit signal rather than drifting into it. ahora en serio, hablando en serio, bueno pues, dicho esto, si me permite, para terminar: one of these opens the second half of the piece, and everybody hears the turn.

The turn moves three things at once. The ADDRESS moves (tú against usted, M3's rows). The FRAME moves (¿me pones? against ¿podría?, L2-M1's rows). And the vocabulary TIER moves (an idiom from M1 against a formula from M4). Move only one and nothing has happened.

Politeness lives in the frame, not in the pronoun. A piece may pivot from formal to intimate and be MORE courteous for it: usted with a blunt frame is colder than tú with ¿te importaría? That is the last thing this course has to say about register.

The small change of key: en plan, digamos and por así decirlo loosen a claim; eso es, exacto, efectivamente and desde luego agree with one, in rising order of formality. Reach for the right tier and the register carries itself.

English carries a change of register almost entirely in TONE and word choice, having no second-person pronoun to move. So a learner writes a piece whose words get longer and whose grammar never shifts, and to a Spanish ear nothing has happened at all.

Direction matters, and English gets it backwards. An English speaker assumes formal to informal is the friendly move and takes it freely; in Spanish, going from usted to tú claims an intimacy that may not be on offer. Going the other way, tú to usted, is a real and legible cooling.

This module opens no system. No new tense, no new mood, no new class of connector. If a piece needs a shape the ladder has not taught, the piece is wrong and not the ladder, and that is the plainest test an exit module has.

sentences.display: Bueno pues, muchas gracias a todos por venir hoy aquí.
sentences.cue: Right then, thank you all very much for coming today.
sentences.literal: Well then, many thanks to all for to-come today here.

words.note: Opens a piece, or restarts one. Both halves are L1-M10's on their own; together they are the sound of somebody taking the floor.

sentences.trap: Bueno pues is not filler even though both words can be. Together they mark a beginning, and a Spanish listener stops talking when they hear it.
sentences.sound: The two words run into one, bwe-no-PWES, with the weight on the second.

variations.display: Pues bueno, muchas gracias a todos.
variations.cue: Well then, thank you all very much.
variations.changed: The two halves reversed, which is just as common and means the same.

variations.display: Muchas gracias a todos por venir.
variations.cue: Thank you all very much for coming.
variations.changed: Without the opener. Correct, and it starts without warning — the listener has to catch up.

mistake.display: Bueno pues muchas gracias a todos por venir aqui hoy.
mistake.why: aquí needs its accent. Without it aqui is not a word, and in a written toast that is the first thing anyone sees.

sentences.usage: Informal, and the opening half of a piece that will turn serious later. This is the voice you use with people you know.
sentences.mnemonic: Take the floor before you use it.

sentences.display: En plan, esto es una boda, no un examen, ¿vale?
sentences.cue: Like, this is a wedding, not an exam, all right?
sentences.literal: In plan, this is a wedding, not an exam, okay?

words.note: Marks the loosest register Spanish has. Fine among friends, badly out of place with anyone you address as usted.

sentences.trap: En plan is the clearest register flag in this module: it cannot appear in the formal half of a piece. If you find yourself writing en plan after si me permite, the piece has come apart.
sentences.sound: En plan is said flat and fast, em-PLAN, with the n before the p sounding like an m.

variations.display: Esto es una boda, no un examen.
variations.cue: This is a wedding, not an exam.
variations.changed: Without the flag. The same joke, now in a neutral voice that would sit anywhere.

variations.display: En plan, esto es una fiesta, ¿vale?
variations.cue: Like, this is a party, right?
variations.changed: The flag with a different noun. What carries the register is en plan, not the content.

mistake.display: Si me permite, en plan, esto es una boda.
mistake.why: Two registers in five words. si me permite belongs to the formal half of a piece and en plan to the informal one; putting them together tells the listener you are not in control of either.

sentences.usage: Informal only, and mostly Peninsular. In much of Latin America the same slot is filled by como que or tipo.

sentences.display: Ahora en serio: gracias por venir aquí con la familia.
sentences.cue: Seriously now: thank you for coming here with the family.
sentences.literal: Now in serious: thanks for to-come here with the family.

words.note: THE pivot of this module. It announces that the joking half is over and buys you the room's attention for the second half.

sentences.trap: This is the single most useful phrase in the module and it does nothing on its own. It only works if what follows actually changes register — the address, the frame, the tier — otherwise it is a promise you do not keep.
sentences.sound: Said as one unit with a small pause after it: a-o-ra-en-SE-ryo, then breathe.

variations.display: Ahora en serio.
variations.cue: Seriously now.
variations.changed: The pivot alone, followed by the pause. That pause is doing half the work.

variations.display: Hablando en serio, gracias por venir.
variations.cue: On a serious note, thank you for coming.
variations.changed: The other pivot, a shade more measured. Either one turns the piece.

mistake.display: Ahora en serio, en plan, gracias por venir aqui.
mistake.why: The pivot promised a change of register and en plan immediately undoes it. And aquí has lost its accent.

sentences.usage: Neutral, and it belongs at the hinge of a piece. Said at the very start it has nothing to turn from.
sentences.mnemonic: Announce the turn, then actually turn.

sentences.display: Hablando en serio, si me permite, quiero agradecer la ayuda.
sentences.cue: On a serious note, if I may, I want to thank you for the help.
sentences.literal: Speaking in serious, if me you-permit, I-want to-thank the help.

words.note: The more measured of the two pivots. ahora en serio turns a joke; this one turns a whole conversation.
Asks the floor rather than taking it, and the verb ending is the register: permite to usted, permites to tú.

sentences.trap: si me permite carries usted inside its verb ending. Saying it to a friend is not more polite, it is a small step backwards, and it is exactly the cooling rule six describes.
sentences.sound: Permite is per-MI-te, and the r is a single tap rather than the rolled one.

variations.display: Si me permites, quiero agradecer la ayuda.
variations.cue: If I may, I want to thank you for the help.
variations.changed: The same frame to tú. One letter moves and the whole piece changes address.

variations.display: Hablando en serio, quiero agradecer la ayuda.
variations.cue: On a serious note, I want to thank you for the help.
variations.changed: The pivot without the request for the floor. Still formal, and now slightly more direct.

mistake.display: Si me permite, tienes razon y te agradezco la ayuda.
mistake.why: The frame opened with usted and the sentence finished with tú. Pick one address and hold it for the whole half; razón also needs its accent.

sentences.usage: Formal, and the second half of a piece that opened informally. This is the voice for a room rather than a table.
sentences.mnemonic: Ask for the floor in the ending of the verb.

sentences.display: Dicho esto, para terminar, brindemos por la familia y los amigos.
sentences.cue: That said, to finish, let us drink to family and friends.
sentences.literal: Said this, for to-finish, let-us-toast for the family and the friends.

words.note: Closes what came before and opens the last part. It concedes nothing; it simply draws a line under the previous half.
Promises the end is one sentence away. Say it and then finish, or the room stops believing you.

sentences.trap: Dicho esto and ahora bien both turn a piece and they turn it differently. M6's ahora bien answers an objection; dicho esto simply closes a section, and nothing is being argued.
sentences.sound: Dicho has the ch of English church: DI-cho, with the stress on the first syllable.

variations.display: Para terminar, brindemos por la familia.
variations.cue: To finish, let us drink to family.
variations.changed: The closing alone, which is enough for a short piece.

variations.display: Dicho esto, brindemos por los amigos.
variations.cue: That said, let us drink to friends.
variations.changed: The line under the previous half, then straight to the toast.

mistake.display: Para terminar, brindemos por la familia, y ahora en serio.
mistake.why: The pivot cannot follow the ending. ahora en serio opens the second half of a piece; after para terminar there is no half left to open.

sentences.usage: Formal to neutral, and the last thing said before a toast. L2-M6's brindemos is doing the work; these two frames only set it up.
sentences.mnemonic: Say para terminar and then terminate.

sentences.display: Digamos que, por así decirlo, ha sido una noche muy larga.
sentences.cue: Let us say that, so to speak, it has been a very long night.
sentences.literal: Let-us-say that, for thus to-say-it, has been a night very long.

words.cue: let us say, shall we say
words.note: Softens the claim that follows without hedging it: you are choosing the word, not doubting the fact.
Flags the words as approximate. It is the mid tier: less casual than en plan, less formal than a written formula.

sentences.trap: These two look like L4-M5's hedges and are not. A hedge softens the claim; these soften the wording, and the claim underneath is as firm as ever.
sentences.sound: Digamos is di-GA-mos, and the g stays hard because it comes before an a.

variations.display: Digamos que ha sido una noche larga.
variations.cue: Let us say it has been a long night.
variations.changed: One softener instead of two, which is what you would actually say.

variations.display: Ha sido una noche muy larga.
variations.cue: It has been a very long night.
variations.changed: Nothing softened at all. The same fact, and now you are standing behind every word of it.

mistake.display: Digamos, en plan, por así decirlo, ha sido larga.
mistake.why: Three softeners from three different tiers in one clause. Choose the tier the half of the piece is in and use one marker from it.

sentences.usage: Neutral, and the safest register in the module: por así decirlo is at home in both halves of a piece.
sentences.mnemonic: Soften the wording, not the claim.

sentences.display: Eso es. Exacto. Es lo que quiero decir, claro.
sentences.cue: That is it. Exactly. That is what I mean, of course.
sentences.literal: That is. Exact. Is the that I-want to-say, clear.

words.note: Agreement at the informal end. L4-M4's eso keeps its own row; the two words together are a whole reply.
A step up from eso es and still ordinary. It agrees with a statement, never with a person.

sentences.trap: Spanish has a ladder of agreements and using the wrong rung is audible. eso es to a friend, exacto in a meeting, efectivamente in writing or to a room — the content is identical and the register is not.
sentences.sound: Exacto is ek-SAK-to, and the x is a k plus an s rather than the English gz.

variations.display: Eso es, exacto.
variations.cue: That is it, exactly.
variations.changed: Two rungs of the ladder side by side, which is how a listener usually agrees twice.

variations.display: Exacto. Es lo que quiero decir.
variations.cue: Exactly. That is what I mean.
variations.changed: Agreement plus M8's repair frame, one tier up from eso es.

mistake.display: Eso es, efectivamente, en plan exacto.
mistake.why: Three rungs of the same ladder at once, and one of them is slang. Agreeing three times in five words reads as nervousness rather than as emphasis.

sentences.usage: Neutral. eso es sits in the informal half of a piece, exacto anywhere, and both are said constantly.

sentences.display: Desde luego, usted tiene razón. Me explico mejor, perdone.
sentences.cue: Of course, you are quite right. Let me put it better, forgive me.
sentences.literal: From then, you have reason. Me I-explain better, forgive.

words.note: The formal rung of the agreement ladder. Nothing to do with time, despite the luego inside it.
Offers a clearer version. No sé si me explico turns it into a question and is a courtesy, not real doubt.

sentences.trap: Desde luego is not later on. Read literally it looks temporal, and it is the most emphatic agreement on the ladder — closer to absolutely than to of course.
sentences.sound: Desde luego runs as DES-de-LWE-go, and the d in the middle is soft, closer to the th of this.

variations.display: Desde luego que sí.
variations.cue: Absolutely.
variations.changed: The strongest form of the agreement, with the que sí doing the emphasis.

variations.display: No sé si me explico.
variations.cue: I am not sure I am making myself clear.
variations.changed: The same offer turned into a question, which is the more courteous half of the pair.

mistake.display: Desde luego, usted tienes razón, me explico.
mistake.why: The address is broken in the middle: usted takes tiene, not tienes. This is exactly what rule two means by holding the address for the whole half.

sentences.usage: Formal. Every word here belongs to the usted half of a piece, and L2-M1's perdone is what closes it.
sentences.mnemonic: Desde luego agrees, it does not wait.

sentences.display: Yo diría que sí, aunque con usted diría que quizá no.
sentences.cue: I would say yes, though with you I would say perhaps not.
sentences.literal: I would-say that yes, although with you would-say that perhaps not.

words.note: The bare conditional of decir. L4-M5's yo diría is the fixed hedge; this is the same form used freely in a clause.

sentences.trap: The two halves of this sentence say the same thing to two different people, and only con usted marks the difference. That is the whole module in one line: the content did not move, the address did.
sentences.sound: Diría is di-RI-a, three syllables, and the accent on the i is what stops it collapsing to dria.

variations.display: Yo diría que sí.
variations.cue: I would say yes.
variations.changed: L4-M5's fixed hedge, unchanged and still doing its old job.

variations.display: Con usted diría que quizá no.
variations.cue: With you I would say perhaps not.
variations.changed: The formal half alone. Same verb, and the address has moved everything.

mistake.display: Yo diria que si, aunque con usted dirias que quiza no.
mistake.why: usted takes diría, not dirías, and three accents are missing. Sí with an accent is yes; si without one is if.

sentences.usage: Neutral, and it is the sentence to keep if you remember nothing else: what you say can stay put while who you are saying it to moves.
sentences.mnemonic: Same words, different person, different Spanish.

sentences.display: Efectivamente, contigo hablo así, y con usted no. Me explico.
sentences.cue: Quite so: with you I talk like this, and with you I do not. Let me explain.
sentences.literal: Effectively, with-you I-speak thus, and with you not. Me I-explain.

words.note: The top rung of the agreement ladder: written Spanish, or a room. Said to a friend it sounds like a parody.

sentences.trap: Contigo and con usted are the same three English words, and in Spanish they are two different relationships. English has no pronoun to move, which is why a learner's piece can change every word and still not change register.
sentences.sound: Efectivamente is long and evenly stressed until the end: e-fek-ti-ba-MEN-te.

variations.display: Contigo hablo así, y con usted no.
variations.cue: With you I talk like this, and with you I do not.
variations.changed: The contrast alone. Nine words, and the entire course's argument about register is inside it.

variations.display: Efectivamente, con usted hablo así.
variations.cue: Quite so, with you I talk like this.
variations.changed: The formal rung with the formal address, matched. That matching is what a finished piece sounds like.

mistake.display: Efectivamente, contigo hablo asi, en plan.
mistake.why: The top rung of the ladder and the bottom one in the same breath, and así without its accent. If the halves of a piece are going to differ, they differ in order, not word by word.

sentences.usage: Formal at the front, informal at the back, deliberately: this last sentence of the course runs both registers in one line so you can hear the seam.

comprehensionPool.display: Bueno pues, muchas gracias a todos.
comprehensionPool.cue: Right then, thank you all very much.

comprehensionPool.display: En plan, esto es una fiesta.
Ahora en serio, gracias por venir.
comprehensionPool.cue: Seriously now, thank you for coming.

comprehensionPool.display: Hablando en serio, quiero agradecer la ayuda.
comprehensionPool.cue: On a serious note, I want to thank you for the help.

comprehensionPool.display: Si me permite, quiero decir unas palabras.
comprehensionPool.cue: If I may, I would like to say a few words.
That said, to finish, let us drink to it.

comprehensionPool.display: Digamos que ha sido una noche larga.
comprehensionPool.cue: Let us say it has been a long night.

comprehensionPool.display: Por así decirlo, no está mal.
comprehensionPool.cue: So to speak, it is not bad at all.
